import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cherlin–Zilber conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Stable group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_group)
-/

namespace CherlinZilberConjecture

open Cardinal FirstOrder
open FirstOrder.Language

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | one : GroupFunc 0
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The first-order language with multiplication, inverse, and identity as its only symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : FirstOrder.Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations := fun _ ↦ Empty

/-- The canonical interpretation of the first-order language of groups on an abstract group. -/
def groupStructure (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap := fun {n} f ↦ match n, f with
    | _, .one => fun _ ↦ 1
    | _, .inv => fun x ↦ (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .mul => fun x ↦ x 0 * x 1
  RelMap := fun {_} r ↦ nomatch r

/-- Two elements have the same complete first-order 1-type over `A` in the pure group language. -/
def SameTypeOver {M : Type*} [Group M] (A : Set M) (x y : M) : Prop :=
  let _ : groupLanguage.Structure M := groupStructure M
  ∀ φ : groupLanguage.Formula (A ⊕ Unit),
    φ.Realize (Sum.elim Subtype.val (fun _ ↦ x)) ↔
      φ.Realize (Sum.elim Subtype.val (fun _ ↦ y))

/-- The setoid identifying elements with the same complete 1-type over a parameter set. -/
def sameTypeSetoid {M : Type*} [Group M] (A : Set M) : Setoid M where
  r := SameTypeOver A
  iseqv := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Iff.rfl, fun h φ ↦ (h φ).symm,
    fun h₁ h₂ φ ↦ (h₁ φ).trans (h₂ φ)⟩

/-- The number of complete 1-types over `A` that are realized in `M`. -/
def numberOfRealizedOneTypes {M : Type*} [Group M] (A : Set M) : Cardinal :=
  Cardinal.mk (Quotient (sameTypeSetoid A))

/-- The complete pure group theory of `G` is omega-stable.

This uses the equivalent characterization that, in every elementarily equivalent group, at most
countably many 1-types over each countable parameter set are realized.
-/
def IsOmegaStableGroup (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  let _ : groupLanguage.Structure G := groupStructure G
  ∀ (M : Type u) (hM : Group M),
    let _ : Group M := hM
    let _ : groupLanguage.Structure M := groupStructure M
    groupLanguage.completeTheory M = groupLanguage.completeTheory G →
      ∀ A : Set M, #A ≤ ℵ₀ → numberOfRealizedOneTypes A ≤ ℵ₀

/-- A subset of affine space cut out by an arbitrary family of polynomial equations. -/
def IsAlgebraicSet {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {n : ℕ} (X : Set (Fin n → K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K),
    X = {x | ∀ p ∈ S, MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0}

/-- Zariski connectedness for an affine algebraic set.

Since the ambient set is algebraic, its relatively closed subsets are again affine algebraic sets,
which permits this separation-based definition without installing a new topology.
-/
def IsZariskiConnected {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {n : ℕ} (X : Set (Fin n → K)) : Prop :=
  X.Nonempty ∧ ∀ A B : Set (Fin n → K), IsAlgebraicSet A → IsAlgebraicSet B →
    A ⊆ X → B ⊆ X → X ⊆ A ∪ B → Disjoint A B → A = ∅ ∨ B = ∅

/-- A concrete affine algebraic group over `K`: an affine algebraic set whose group operations are
regular maps, represented coordinatewise by polynomials. -/
structure AffineAlgebraicGroup (K : Type*) [Field K] where
  n : ℕ
  carrier : Set (Fin n → K)
  isAlgebraic : IsAlgebraicSet carrier
  group : Group carrier
  mul_polynomial : ∃ p : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n ⊕ Fin n) K,
    ∀ x y : carrier, ∀ i,
      ((group.mul x y : carrier) : Fin n → K) i =
        MvPolynomial.eval (Sum.elim (x : Fin n → K) (y : Fin n → K)) (p i)
  inv_polynomial : ∃ p : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) K,
    ∀ x : carrier, ∀ i,
      ((group.inv x : carrier) : Fin n → K) i = MvPolynomial.eval x (p i)

/-- A connected, positive-dimensional, simple affine algebraic group.

Here positive-dimensionality is expressed by infinitude of the algebraic set, an equivalent
condition for affine algebraic sets of finite type over an algebraically closed field. Algebraic
simplicity means noncommutativity and absence of a proper nontrivial connected normal algebraic
subgroup.
-/
def AffineAlgebraicGroup.IsSimple {K : Type*} [Field K] (A : AffineAlgebraicGroup K) : Prop :=
  letI : Group A.carrier := A.group
  IsZariskiConnected A.carrier ∧ A.carrier.Infinite ∧
    (¬ ∀ x y : A.carrier, x * y = y * x) ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup A.carrier, H.Normal →
      IsAlgebraicSet (((fun x : A.carrier ↦ (x : Fin A.n → K)) '' (H : Set A.carrier))) →
      IsZariskiConnected (((fun x : A.carrier ↦ (x : Fin A.n → K)) '' (H : Set A.carrier))) →
      H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

/-- **Cherlin–Zilber conjecture.** Every infinite nonabelian simple group whose complete
first-order theory in the pure language of groups is $\omega$-stable is isomorphic, as an abstract
group, to the group of points of a connected positive-dimensional simple algebraic group over an
algebraically closed field.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : ¬ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x) (hstable : IsOmegaStableGroup G) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (A : AffineAlgebraicGroup K),
      A.IsSimple ∧ (letI : Group A.carrier := A.group; Nonempty (G ≃* A.carrier)) := by
  sorry

end CherlinZilberConjecture
modeling_decisions: Following the Stable group article and the fixed decomposition, the source's terse “simple group” is formalized as an infinite nonabelian abstract simple group; infinitude excludes finite simple groups, which otherwise have omega-stable theories.

“Stable in aleph_0” is read as omega-stable, not merely stable or superstable. It is encoded by the standard equivalent criterion that every group elementarily equivalent to G realizes at most countably many complete 1-types over each countable parameter set.
The first-order theory is taken in the pure language of groups, with multiplication, inverse, identity, and built-in equality.

Because Mathlib has no algebraic-group or group-scheme primitive, an algebraic group is represented concretely as a Zariski-closed subset of finite-dimensional affine space whose multiplication and inversion are coordinatewise polynomial. Connected algebraic groups are affine varieties in the intended simple linear-algebraic-group setting, so this concrete presentation does not restrict the conjecture's intended conclusion.
Algebraic simplicity is modeled in the standard connected sense: the group is connected and noncommutative and has no proper nontrivial connected normal closed algebraic subgroup.
Positive dimension is represented by infinitude of the affine algebraic set. For finite-type affine algebraic sets over an algebraically closed field, this is equivalent to positive dimension.
The conclusion uses an abstract group isomorphism from G to the full K-point group of the represented algebraic group.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cherlin–Zilber conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Stable group*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_group)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [G. Cherlin, *Groups of small Morley rank*, Ann. Math. Logic 17 (1979), 1–28](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4843(79)90019-6)
- [B. I. Zil'ber, *Groups and rings whose theory is categorical*, Fundam. Math. 95 (1977), 173–188](https://doi.org/10.4064/fm-95-3-173-188)
- [T. Altınel, A. V. Borovik, G. Cherlin, *Simple groups of finite Morley rank*, AMS (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1090/surv/145)

The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture (also called the *algebraicity conjecture*) states that an infinite
simple group whose first-order theory is stable in $\aleph_0$ (i.e. $\omega$-stable) is a simple
algebraic group over an algebraically closed field.

Mathlib has neither $\omega$-stability nor algebraic groups, so this file defines both.

* `Language.group` is the first-order language of groups; every group is a structure for it.
* A theory `T` is $\omega$-stable (`IsOmegaStable`) if for every model `M` of `T` and every
  countable set `A ⊆ M` of parameters, there are only countably many complete types over `A`.
* Algebraic groups over an algebraically closed field `K` are modelled as Zariski-closed subgroups
  of `GL n K`. This loses no generality: a simple algebraic group is non-commutative, hence affine
  by Chevalley's structure theorem, hence isomorphic to a closed subgroup of some `GL n K`.
  A closed subgroup is *connected* if it has no proper closed subgroup of finite index, and it is a
  *simple algebraic group* if it is connected, non-commutative, and has no connected closed normal
  subgroups other than the trivial subgroup and itself.
-/

namespace CherlinZilberConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: a binary multiplication, a unary
inversion and a constant for the identity. -/
inductive groupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : groupFunc 2
  | inv : groupFunc 1
  | one : groupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups, with function symbols `*`, `⁻¹` and `1` and no relation
symbols. -/
def Language.group : Language :=
  { Functions := groupFunc
    Relations := fun _ => Empty }

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the symbols by the group
operations. -/
instance {G : Type*} [Group G] : Language.group.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => 1
  RelMap {_} r := r.elim

section groupStructure

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_mul (x : Fin 2 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) groupFunc.mul x = x 0 * x 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_inv (x : Fin 1 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) groupFunc.inv x = (x 0)⁻¹ := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_one (x : Fin 0 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) groupFunc.one x = 1 := rfl

end groupStructure

/-- A first-order theory `T` is *$\omega$-stable* (or *stable in $\aleph_0$*) if for every model
`M` of `T`, every countable set `A ⊆ M` of parameters and every `m`, there are only countably many
complete `m`-types over `A`, i.e. the complete theory of `M` in the language `L[[A]]` with a
constant for each element of `A` has only countably many complete types in `m` variables.

As for `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`, the models range over `Type (max u v)`. By the
downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this loses no generality: the types over a countable set `A` in
a model `M` only depend on the complete theory of `M` in the language `L[[A]]`, which is shared by
any countable elementary substructure of `M` containing `A`. -/
def IsOmegaStable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (A : Set M), A.Countable →
    ∀ m : ℕ, Countable ((L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin m))

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is *Zariski-closed* if it is the set of common zeros in `GL n K` of
an ideal of polynomials in the matrix entries. -/
def IsZariskiClosed (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K),
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) K, g ∈ H ↔ (fun ij => g.val ij.1 ij.2) ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus K I

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_top : IsZariskiClosed (⊤ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨⊥, fun _ => by simp⟩

open MvPolynomial in
@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_bot : IsZariskiClosed (⊥ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) := by
  refine ⟨Ideal.span (Set.range fun ij : Fin n × Fin n =>
    X ij - C ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) ij.1 ij.2)), fun g => ?_⟩
  rw [zeroLocus_span, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Subgroup.mem_bot, Units.ext_iff, Units.val_one]
  simp only [Set.forall_mem_range, map_sub, aeval_X, aeval_C, Algebra.algebraMap_self,
    RingHom.id_apply, sub_eq_zero]
  exact ⟨fun h ij => by rw [h], fun h => Matrix.ext fun i j => h (i, j)⟩

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is *Zariski-connected* if it has no Zariski-closed subgroup of finite
index other than itself. For a Zariski-closed subgroup `H` this is equivalent to connectedness in
the Zariski topology, since the identity component of `H` is a closed subgroup of finite index
contained in every closed subgroup of finite index. -/
def IsZariskiConnected (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∀ H' ≤ H, IsZariskiClosed H' → (H'.subgroupOf H).FiniteIndex → H' = H

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiConnected_bot : IsZariskiConnected (⊥ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) :=
  fun _ h _ _ => le_bot_iff.mp h

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is a *simple (linear) algebraic group* if it is Zariski-closed,
connected, non-commutative, and its only connected Zariski-closed normal subgroups are the
trivial subgroup and `H` itself. -/
def IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  IsZariskiClosed H ∧ IsZariskiConnected H ∧ ¬ IsMulCommutative H ∧
    ∀ N ≤ H, IsZariskiClosed N → IsZariskiConnected N → (N.subgroupOf H).Normal →
      N = ⊥ ∨ N = H

/-- **Cherlin–Zilber conjecture.** An infinite simple group $G$ whose first-order theory (in the
language of groups) is stable in $\aleph_0$, i.e. $\omega$-stable, is a simple algebraic group over
an algebraically closed field: there are an algebraically closed field $K$ and a simple algebraic
group $H$ over $K$, realised as a Zariski-closed subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, such that $G$ is
isomorphic (as an abstract group) to the group $H(K)$ of $K$-points of $H$.

The hypothesis that $G$ is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose theories are trivially
$\omega$-stable. An infinite simple group is automatically non-abelian. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : IsOmegaStable (Language.group.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end CherlinZilberConjecture

modeling_decisions: Added the implicit hypothesis `[Infinite G]` (from the Wikipedia article: 'infinite (ω-stable) simple groups'); without it the statement is false for finite simple groups. Non-abelianness is not added since an infinite simple group is automatically non-abelian.

'First-order theory' is taken as the complete theory `Language.group.completeTheory G` of G in the language of groups (symbols *, ⁻¹, 1, plus built-in equality), a bespoke language defined in the file in the style of Mathlib's `Language.ring`.

'Stable in ℵ₀' is formalized as ω-stability: for every model M of T, every countable parameter set A ⊆ M and every m, the set of complete m-types over A (Mathlib's `CompleteType` of the complete theory of M in the language L[[A]], in variables `Fin m`) is countable. Quantifying over all m rather than only 1-types is the standard (Marker-style) definition and is equivalent to the 1-type version.

Following Mathlib's convention for `Theory.IsSatisfiable`/`IsComplete`, models in `IsOmegaStable` range over `Type (max u v)` (here `Type 0`). By downward Löwenheim–Skolem this loses no generality (types over a countable A depend only on the L[[A]]-theory of M, shared with a countable elementary substructure containing A).

'Simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field' is modelled concretely as a Zariski-closed subgroup H of GL n K with K algebraically closed (linear algebraic group in the classical, K-points sense), since every simple algebraic group is non-commutative, hence affine (Chevalley), hence linear. G is required to be isomorphic as an abstract group to H = H(K).

Zariski-closedness of a subgroup of GL n K is expressed via `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` of an ideal in the n² matrix-entry variables; this is correct because GL n is an open subvariety of affine n²-space, so its Zariski topology is the subspace topology.

Connectedness of a closed subgroup is defined as 'no proper Zariski-closed subgroup of finite index', a standard characterization (the identity component is a closed subgroup of finite index contained in every closed subgroup of finite index; the Wikipedia article itself uses this form of the definition). Simplicity uses the standard 'connected, non-commutative, no proper nontrivial connected closed normal subgroups'. Note that since G is abstractly simple and infinite, any Zariski-closed subgroup of GL n K isomorphic to G automatically satisfies all these conditions, so the truth value of the statement is insensitive to these convention choices (e.g. 'simple' vs 'almost simple', or connected vs arbitrary closed normal subgroups).

K is required to live in the same universe as G (`K : Type u`). This is no restriction: |K| ≤ |G| whenever G ≅ H(K) for an infinite closed subgroup H of GL n K, so K can always be transported to universe u.

  ∃ equations : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K),

def IsAffineIrreducible {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {n : ℕ} (s : Set (Fin n → K)) : Prop :=

  ambientDimension : ℕ

  /-- The carrier is an algebraic set. -/
  isAlgebraic : IsAffineAlgebraicSet carrier
  /-- The group law on the `K`-points. -/
  [group : Group ↥carrier]

Mathlib has neither the first-order language of groups, nor ω-stability, nor algebraic groups.

* the language of groups has function symbols for multiplication, inversion and the identity;
* a theory `T` is ω-stable if for every model `M` of `T` and every countable set of parameters
  `A ⊆ M` there are only countably many complete types over `A`;
* an algebraic group over `K` is a Zariski closed subgroup of some `GL n K`, i.e. a linear
  algebraic group. Simple algebraic groups are affine, hence linear, so this loses no generality.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wikipedia, Stable group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_group)
* [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
* G. Cherlin, *Groups of small Morley rank*, Ann. Math. Logic 17 (1979), 1–28.
-/

namespace CherlinZilberConjecture

open FirstOrder Language Matrix
open scoped MatrixGroups

section LanguageOfGroups

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: multiplication, inversion and the
identity. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | one : GroupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups, with function symbols `*`, `⁻¹` and `1` and no relation
symbols. -/
def Language.group : FirstOrder.Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- A group `G` is a structure for the language of groups in the canonical way. -/
instance instGroupStructure (G : Type*) [Group G] : Language.group.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => 1
  RelMap {_} r _ := r.elim

end LanguageOfGroups

section OmegaStability

/-- A first-order theory `T` is *ω-stable* (also called $\aleph_0$-stable, or "stable in
$\aleph_0$") if for every model `M` of `T`, every countable set of parameters `A ⊆ M` and every
`n`, there are only countably many complete `n`-types over `A`. Here a complete `n`-type over `A`
is a complete type of the theory of `M` in the language `L[[A]]` expanded by constants for the
elements of `A`. -/
def IsOmegaStable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (A : Set M), A.Countable →
    ∀ n : ℕ, Countable ((L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin n))

end OmegaStability

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type*} [Field K]

def IsZariskiClosed (H : Subgroup (GL n K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (MvPolynomial (n × n) K), ∀ g : GL n K,

Zariski closed subgroup of finite index other than itself. For a Zariski closed subgroup this is
equivalent to being connected (equivalently, irreducible) in the Zariski topology. -/
def IsZariskiConnected (H : Subgroup (GL n K)) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : Subgroup (GL n K), IsZariskiClosed N → N ≤ H → N.IsFiniteRelIndex H → N = H

  · rintro rfl i j

  · intro h

    exact h i j

group whose first-order theory is stable in $\aleph_0$ (i.e. $\omega$-stable) is a simple
algebraic group over an algebraically closed field.

- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

- G. Cherlin, *Groups of small Morley rank*, Ann. Math. Logic 17 (1979), 1–28.
- B. I. Zil'ber, *Groups and rings whose theory is categorical*, Fundam. Math. 95 (1977),

namespace CherlinZilberConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Matrix
open scoped MatrixGroups

universe u v

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: a binary multiplication,
a unary inversion and a constant for the identity. -/
inductive groupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : groupFunc 2
  | inv : groupFunc 1
  | one : groupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups $(\cdot, {}^{-1}, 1)$. It has no relation symbols. -/
def Language.group : Language where
  Functions := groupFunc
  Relations := fun _ => Empty

/-- A group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the symbols by the group
operations. -/
instance {G : Type*} [Group G] : Language.group.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1
  RelMap r := r.elim

/-- The multiplication symbol is interpreted by the multiplication of the group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_mul {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : Fin 2 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) (groupFunc.mul : Language.group.Functions 2) x =
      x 0 * x 1 := rfl

/-- The inversion symbol is interpreted by the inversion of the group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_inv {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : Fin 1 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) (groupFunc.inv : Language.group.Functions 1) x =
      (x 0)⁻¹ := rfl

/-- The constant symbol is interpreted by the identity of the group. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_one {G : Type*} [Group G] (x : Fin 0 → G) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.group) (groupFunc.one : Language.group.Functions 0) x =
      1 := rfl

/-- A first-order theory `T` is *$\omega$-stable* (also called $\aleph_0$-stable, or "stable
in $\aleph_0$") if for every model `M` of `T` and every countable set `A` of parameters from `M`
there are only countably many complete $1$-types over `A`. Here a complete $1$-type over `A`
is a complete type in one variable of the complete theory of `M` in the language `L[[A]]`
obtained from `L` by adding a constant symbol for each element of `A`. -/
def IsOmegaStable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (A : Set M), A.Countable →
    Countable ((L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType Unit)

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is *Zariski closed* if it consists of the invertible matrices at
which all polynomials of some ideal of polynomials in the matrix entries vanish. Zariski closed
subgroups of `GL n K` are the (linear) algebraic groups over `K` in the classical sense; every
affine algebraic group over `K` is isomorphic to one of them. -/
def IsZariskiClosed (H : Subgroup (GL n K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (n × n) K),
    ∀ g : GL n K, g ∈ H ↔
      (fun ij : n × n => (g : Matrix n n K) ij.1 ij.2) ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus K I

/-- A Zariski closed subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is *connected* if it has no proper Zariski closed
subgroup of finite index. (The identity component of an algebraic group is a Zariski closed
subgroup of finite index, and a Zariski closed subgroup of finite index is also open.) -/
def IsConnectedZariskiClosed (H : Subgroup (GL n K)) : Prop :=
  IsZariskiClosed H ∧ ∀ H' ≤ H, IsZariskiClosed H' → H'.relIndex H ≠ 0 → H' = H

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL n K` is a *simple algebraic group* if it is Zariski closed, connected
and noncommutative, and it has no connected Zariski closed normal subgroups other than the
trivial subgroup and `H` itself. -/
structure IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL n K)) : Prop where
  isConnectedZariskiClosed : IsConnectedZariskiClosed H
  not_isMulCommutative : ¬ IsMulCommutative H
  eq_bot_or_eq_of_normal : ∀ N ≤ H, IsConnectedZariskiClosed N → (N.subgroupOf H).Normal →
    N = ⊥ ∨ N = H

/-- The whole group `GL n K` is Zariski closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_top : IsZariskiClosed (⊤ : Subgroup (GL n K)) :=
  ⟨⊥, fun _ => by simp⟩

/-- The trivial subgroup of `GL n K` is Zariski closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_bot : IsZariskiClosed (⊥ : Subgroup (GL n K)) := by
  refine ⟨Ideal.span (Set.range fun ij : n × n =>
    MvPolynomial.X ij - MvPolynomial.C ((1 : Matrix n n K) ij.1 ij.2)), fun g => ?_⟩
  simp only [MvPolynomial.zeroLocus_span, Subgroup.mem_bot, Set.mem_setOf_eq,
    Set.forall_mem_range, map_sub, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, MvPolynomial.aeval_C,
    Algebra.algebraMap_self, RingHom.id_apply, sub_eq_zero, Prod.forall]
  constructor
  · rintro rfl i j
    rfl
  · intro h
    exact Units.ext (Matrix.ext h)

/-- The trivial subgroup of `GL n K` is connected. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isConnectedZariskiClosed_bot : IsConnectedZariskiClosed (⊥ : Subgroup (GL n K)) :=
  ⟨isZariskiClosed_bot, fun _ hH' _ _ => le_bot_iff.mp hH'⟩

/-- The trivial subgroup of `GL n K` is not a simple algebraic group. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem not_isSimpleAlgebraicGroup_bot : ¬ IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (⊥ : Subgroup (GL n K)) :=
  fun h => h.not_isMulCommutative inferInstance

(in the language of groups) is stable in $\aleph_0$, i.e. $\omega$-stable. Then `G` is a simple
algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: there are an algebraically closed field `K`
and a Zariski closed subgroup `H` of some `GL n K` that is a simple algebraic group, such that
`G` is isomorphic to `H` as an abstract group.

The hypothesis that `G` is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose first-order
theories are trivially $\omega$-stable. An infinite simple group is automatically nonabelian. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 14 20]

    (hG : IsOmegaStable (Language.group.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type*) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end CherlinZilberConjecture

/- ### The first-order language of groups -/

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: `1`, `⁻¹` and `*`. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | one : GroupFunc 0
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | mul : GroupFunc 2

/-- The first-order language of groups: the function symbols `1`, `⁻¹`, `*` and no relation
symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : FirstOrder.Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- The constant symbol `1` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev oneFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 0 := GroupFunc.one

/-- The unary function symbol `⁻¹` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev invFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 1 := GroupFunc.inv

/-- The binary function symbol `*` of the language of groups. -/
abbrev mulFunc : groupLanguage.Functions 2 := GroupFunc.mul

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the symbols by the group
operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f x :=
    match n, f with
    | _, GroupFunc.one => 1
    | _, GroupFunc.inv => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, GroupFunc.mul => x 0 * x 1
  RelMap {_} r _ := (r : Empty).elim

section GroupStructure

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_oneFunc (x : Fin 0 → G) : Structure.funMap oneFunc x = 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_invFunc (a : G) : Structure.funMap invFunc ![a] = a⁻¹ := rfl

@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_mulFunc (a b : G) : Structure.funMap mulFunc ![a, b] = a * b := rfl

end GroupStructure

/- ### Simple algebraic groups -/

section AlgebraicGroup

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/-- A set of `n × n` matrices over `K` is *Zariski closed* if it is the common zero set of a family
of polynomials in the `n²` matrix entries. -/
def IsZariskiClosed (S : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) K),
    S = {A | ∀ p ∈ P, MvPolynomial.eval (fun ij ↦ A ij.1 ij.2) p = 0}

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_univ : IsZariskiClosed (Set.univ : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨∅, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isZariskiClosed_empty : IsZariskiClosed (∅ : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨{1}, by simp⟩

/-- The Zariski topology on `n × n` matrices over `K`: the topology whose closed sets are the
Zariski closed sets. -/
def zariskiTopology : TopologicalSpace (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) :=
  TopologicalSpace.generateFrom {U | IsZariskiClosed Uᶜ}

/-- The set of matrices underlying a subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)`. -/
def matrixSet (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) :=
  ((↑) : GL (Fin n) K → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) '' H

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *linear algebraic group* if it is Zariski closed in
`GL_n(K)`, i.e. it consists of the invertible matrices lying in some Zariski closed set of
matrices. -/
def IsAlgebraicSubgroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ Z : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), IsZariskiClosed Z ∧
    ∀ g : GL (Fin n) K, g ∈ H ↔ (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) ∈ Z

@[category test, AMS 14 20]
theorem isAlgebraicSubgroup_top : IsAlgebraicSubgroup (⊤ : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isZariskiClosed_univ, by simp⟩

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is *connected* if it is connected as a subspace of `GL_n(K)` for
the Zariski topology. -/
def IsZariskiConnected (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  letI := zariskiTopology (K := K) (n := n)
  IsConnected (matrixSet H)

/-- A subgroup `H` of `GL_n(K)` is a *simple algebraic group* if it is a connected noncommutative
linear algebraic group whose only connected closed normal subgroups are the trivial group and `H`
itself. -/
def IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraicSubgroup H ∧ IsZariskiConnected H ∧
    (¬ ∀ a ∈ H, ∀ b ∈ H, a * b = b * a) ∧
    ∀ N : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K), N ≤ H → IsAlgebraicSubgroup N → IsZariskiConnected N →
      (∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N) → N = ⊥ ∨ N = H

end AlgebraicGroup

/--
**The Cherlin–Zilber conjecture** (algebraicity conjecture). Let $G$ be an infinite simple group
whose complete first-order theory (in the language of groups) is $\omega$-stable. Then $G$ is a
simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field: there are an algebraically closed field
$K$ and a simple algebraic group $H \le \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ over $K$ such that $G \cong H$ as
abstract groups.

The hypothesis that $G$ is infinite excludes the finite simple groups, whose theories are
trivially $\omega$-stable.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem cherlin_zilber_conjecture (G : Type u) [Group G] [Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]
    (hG : IsOmegaStable (groupLanguage.completeTheory G)) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K) (n : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) K)),
      IsSimpleAlgebraicGroup H ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end CherlinZilberConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Simple group' + implicit 'infinite' (from the Stable_group article: 'infinite (ω-stable) simple groups') formalized as `[Infinite G] [IsSimpleGroup G]`; the finite case is excluded because finite simple groups are ω-stable but are not connected algebraic groups.

'Stable in ℵ₀' read as ω-stability of the complete theory `groupLanguage.completeTheory G` (Th(G) in the language {1, ⁻¹, *}). ω-stability is defined textbook-style (Marker Def. 4.2.17 / Tent–Ziegler): for every model M, every countable parameter set A ⊆ M and every n, the space S_n^M(A) of complete n-types over A is countable; S_n^M(A) is realised as `(L[[A]].completeTheory M).CompleteType (Fin n)`. Using all n rather than only n = 1 is a standard equivalent choice.

Following Mathlib's convention for `IsSatisfiable`/`ModelsBoundedFormula`, models in `IsOmegaStable` range over `ModelType.{u, v, max u v}` (here `Type 0`); by Löwenheim–Skolem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.

'Simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field' formalized concretely as a Zariski-closed subgroup H of GL_n(K) (K algebraically closed, any n) that is connected in the Zariski topology, noncommutative, and whose closed connected normal subgroups are only ⊥ and H (Humphreys/Borel definition; the variant that also forbids finite normal subgroups is equivalent here because G ≅ H is abstractly simple). Every affine algebraic group is a closed subgroup of some GL_n, and a simple algebraic group is affine, so nothing is lost. Under the hypotheses on G these algebraic-side conditions are in fact automatic for any closed H ≅ G, so the statement is robust to the choice of variant.

The Zariski topology on n×n matrices is defined as `TopologicalSpace.generateFrom` of the complements of Zariski-closed sets (common zero sets of sets of polynomials in the n² entries); since Zariski-closed sets are closed under finite unions and arbitrary intersections this is exactly the Zariski topology. Closed subgroups of GL_n(K) are those of the form {g ∈ GL_n(K) | g ∈ Z} with Z Zariski-closed in M_n(K).
The isomorphism is of abstract groups: `Nonempty (G ≃* H)`. The field K is quantified in the same universe as G (`Type u`); this is harmless since |K| ≤ |G| for any such H(K) ≅ G.
Normality of N in H is written explicitly as ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ x ∈ N, h * x * h⁻¹ ∈ N.
